claim: On 25 November 2026 Ofgem announces a default tariff (energy price) cap for 1 January – 31 March 2027 of at least £2,154 a year for a typical dual-fuel household paying by Direct Debit, i.e. a rise of at least 25% on the current £1,723.

runs.scenario: If the fallback applies and two named sources report figures on opposite sides of the threshold—for example, £2,153 and £2,154—the criterion does not say which source takes precedence.
runs.yes_requires: Within the specified window on 25 November 2026 UK time, Ofgem must announce the cap for 1 January–31 March 2027, with an annual figure of at least £2,154 for a typical dual-fuel household paying by Direct Debit, using Ofgem’s typical domestic consumption values.
runs.decided_by: The annual pound figure in Ofgem’s announcement or its Summary of changes. If Ofgem’s page gives only a percentage, the fallback is the same-day pound figure reported from Ofgem’s documents by Cornwal

runs.yes_requires: Ofgem must announce the 1 Jan – 31 Mar 2027 default tariff cap on 25 November 2026 (UK time), and the stated annual cost for a typical dual-fuel household paying by Direct Debit must be £2,154 or more.
runs.decided_by: Ofgem's official announcement or 'Summary of changes' document, or if only a percentage is given there, same-day reports of Ofgem's figures by Cornwall Insight, the BBC, or the Guardian.

runs.scenario: Ofgem’s page gives only a percentage, and the same day the BBC reports £2,154 while the Guardian reports £2,153, both from Ofgem’s documents; or the Summary of changes states £2,153.50. The criterion lists those outlets with ‘or’ and covers only £2,154 or more versus £2,153 or less, so one careful reader can resolve YES and another NO on the same facts.
